FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `bench/cdsfl_registry/engine.py`, `PolicyEngine.validate()` does not enforce the schema field `min_layer` at all, so the facade’s advertised “minimum layer” constraint is non-functional. Evidence: `min_layer` is parsed in `load_schema()` into each `ParameterDef`, but the only consumers are metadata-returning methods (`list_parameters()`, `get_schema_for()`, `get_parameter()`). In `validate()`, the code delegates to `validate_all_policies()` and then performs only HARD-coverage checks; there is no scan comparing where a parameter is defined versus `defn.min_layer`. Therefore a parameter declared with `min_layer = "model"` can still be set in `universal.toml`, `domain`, or `task` with no error from the engine, and a parameter declared `min_layer = "domain"` can be defined in `universal.toml` with no detection. This directly contradicts the schema contract comment: `min_layer = "lowest layer that may define it"`.
FOLLOW: This is downstream-visible in all configuration hygiene workflows. `validate()` can report success while the repository contains placements the schema says are illegal. Because `query()` and `get_parameter()` trust merged TOML as authoritative, misplaced values still take effect at runtime, so the engine both fails to catch the violation and applies the violating config. This also weakens provenance usefulness: provenance may correctly say `universal`, but the schema simultaneously says the parameter must not exist there. The defect is architectural because one of the facade’s core promises—schema enforcement over the 4-layer hierarchy—is absent.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX: add explicit per-layer `min_layer` validation in `validate()` by scanning each config file and rejecting parameters defined above their allowed minimum layer.

DESCRIPTION: FIND: `bench/cdsfl_registry/engine.py`, `load_schema()` silently accepts unknown parameter definitions in repository config files because `validate()` never checks for dotpaths present in TOML overlays that are absent from `schema.toml`. Evidence: `validate()` only calls `validate_all_policies()` from `registry.py` plus HARD-coverage checks. `validate_all_policies()` checks monotonicity only; it has no schema awareness. `query()` and `diff_policies()` flatten and return whatever keys exist in merged TOML. Therefore a typo like `convergense.v_comp_threshold = 0.7` or a stray unsupported knob is neither rejected nor surfaced as an error; it is simply omitted from schema-driven introspection while still living in the effective merged dict.
FOLLOW: This causes silent misconfiguration on the happy path. A human reviewer can believe they configured a parameter because the TOML file contains it, while `get_parameter("convergence.v_comp_threshold", ...)` continues returning the inherited/default value. Meanwhile `query().effective` still contains the unknown misspelled key, so different API surfaces disagree on the effective policy namespace. This breaks the facade’s claim that the schema is the single source of truth and makes typo-induced no-ops hard to detect.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX: extend `validate()` to flag any config dotpath not present in `self._schema`.

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.73
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `bench/cdsfl_registry/schema.toml` is internally inconsistent with its own header comment for `min_layer`. The header says `Layer: lowest layer that may define this parameter`, but multiple entries use `min_layer = "universal"` for obviously lower-layer-specific knobs such as `[convergence.v_comp_threshold]`, `[convergence.v_struct_threshold]`, `[verification.sympy_timeout_seconds]`, `[verification.sympy_sandbox]`, `[protocol.max_rounds]`, and all `[refinements.*]`. Under the documented meaning, `universal` means those parameters may be defined at any layer, not that they belong to the universal layer. By contrast, model-specific fields correctly use `min_layer = "model"`, which shows the file is trying to encode placement rules, not origin/default location. The semantic problem is that many non-global knobs are marked with the broadest possible scope, so the schema cannot express or enforce intended layer discipline.
FOLLOW: Even after F001 adds enforcement, these entries will remain effectively unrestricted because `universal` is the least restrictive value. That means schema-based validation still cannot catch accidental domain/task/model placement errors for parameters that are probably meant to be constrained more tightly. This is especially relevant for timeouts and protocol/refinement settings that are likely task/model tunables in practice. The issue is not that the current values are illegal TOML; it is that the schema metadata is too weak to support the engine feature it claims to provide.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX: correct the misleading schema header so it matches actual semantics currently encoded by the file, rather than pretending these entries are placement-restricted when many are intentionally unrestricted.

DESCRIPTION: FIND: `bench/cdsfl_registry/engine.py`, `validate()` misclassifies schema HARD string coverage by excluding `type = "enum"` from the schema side while registry enforcement treats all exact-match string-like values the same. Evidence: the current code computes `schema_hard_strings` with `defn.type == "string"`, but `VALID_TYPES` includes `"enum"` and `HARD_STRINGS` in `registry.py` is just a dotpath→str exact-match map with no awareness of schema type. If a future schema entry is defined as `type = "enum"` and marked HARD, `validate()` will incorrectly report it as missing from schema coverage or fail to detect reverse mismatches, even though the registry would enforce it via `HARD_STRINGS`.
FOLLOW: This is a latent but real correctness defect in the schema-enforcement facade. It makes the coverage check non-extensible and creates a false negative/false positive path as soon as any HARD exact-match parameter uses the supported `enum` type. Codex already extended C0004 on malformed enum metadata; this is the complementary runtime coverage mismatch. It also means keeping `"enum"` in `VALID_TYPES` without updating coverage logic leaves the engine internally inconsistent today.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX: treat `"enum"` as string-like in HARD string coverage checks.
